posts.body:
SYNOPSIS
​
The rise of a revolt was inevitable, and to protect the lead researcher of the project and his family, Kairós sent them to a humble house in the mountains, keeping them far from any potential crossfire in case Canaã Cinzento decided to strike.
After the launch of the New Energy Matrix project led by the city of Kairós, the people of Canaã Cinzento watched their forests burn, their rivers become polluted, and their air grow heavier each day—all sacrificed in the name of progress.
But it wasn’t only the citizens’ lives that were affected. Nature itself suffered deeply. For a long time, stories of magical beings had faded away, yet they still existed. Not only for those who believed in them, but also for those who harmed them. The disturbance caused by Kairós’s machines forced the so-called Entities to intervene once more, fighting to protect their home from human hands.
But you’re just a little girl. There’s no way to fully face something beyond your understanding.
So what will you do? Destroy them, or…
CHARACTERS
​
Diana
This is our heroine! a sixteen-year-old girl, daughter of the chief engineer and lead researcher of Kairós’s new project.
Her life had been that of an ordinary teenager in the wealthy city of Kairós, until everything changed. Suddenly, she was forced to move to a small shack in the mountains, seeking refuge from something she didn’t even understand.
One day, while bringing flowers to her mother’s grave atop a hill, she was pushed off it — only to be saved by a mysterious figure.
Vanessa
Diana’s savior. A woman who appears to be around twenty-eight, yet carries an air of mystery.
She seems to know Diana, but the feeling isn’t mutual. Despite the strange circumstances of their first meeting, she enjoys teasing Diana and getting under her skin whenever she can.
A...Child?!
A… child?! His appearance is unlike anyone else’s, and he carries a strange aura. He seems to harbor a deep hatred for Diana, even though she has never met him.
GAMEPLAY
​
Ancestral Future
is a puzzle RPG focused on exploration, where the only battles are boss encounters—also solved through puzzles.
Progress through this world as you uncover its mysteries, its conflicts, and your own place within it.
As the daughter of engineers, you grew up fascinated by all kinds of disciplines. With experience handling many different tools, use them to overcome obstacles and solve puzzles as you advance through the story.
​
Features
Equip the right tool to solve specific puzzles
Defeat bosses by completing puzzles on the battlefield
Some puzzles—including boss fights—can be solved in more than one way
Explore and re-explore areas to uncover more of the story
IMAGES/SCREENSHOTS
Spoiler
BATTLE SYSTEM
Spoiler
The battle system reflects Diana’s own abilities. She’s just a teenager—her only “superpower” is her intelligence. So you’ll need to interact with elements on the battlefield while dodging the boss’s attacks, looking for ways to deal damage indirectly.
Since the Entities act as avatars of nature, you can choose to increase the level of environmental degradation to destroy them… or find another way to overcome the challenge.
The second option isn’t always obvious, so pay close attention to dialogue and to elements in the environment to figure out what to do.

posts.body:
Hey hey hey,
I just played through the demo and I have to say, it was really enjoyable overall! Usually I am not really into puzzles, but this kind of point-and-click-adventure gameplay paired with the Steam Punk Setting got me
I really liked the music, especially at the start of the game. You could use that piece more often^^ The mapping of the broken down factory was also nice, really had this Steam Punk atmosphere.
Regarding the puzzles, I don't think you have to give so many clues in Dianas Dialogue (things like "I should look around for a screwdriver", etc. ), it's easy enough with the symbols. Also sometimes she directly adresses the player in a  "Can you figure that out?" way. Those I would completely cut, because they break the immersion.
That aside, you had some quite nice functions with the puzzles: Talking about the Aether Steel Bender. Il loved that thing
Also really could that I could manually move the Drill Bot, instead of that being just a cutscene, even if it was just a short ride. Maybe you can play a little animation, when it drills through the wall instead of just fading out? Not necessarily pixel art of the bot drilling through, but just little earth animation on the wall? MV has a pretty nice tool to create your own animations.
And for my last suggestion, maybe you want to use another font and exchange some of the default menu sound effects. Of course I am talking as someone who uses the RPG Maker myself, so it's probably because I hear/see them so often, but customizing little things like these can add a lot to your game, in my opinion.
You may also want to go through the localization again. A whole bunch of the dialogue boxes where not translated and those who were often had text, exceeding the window. I'll attach screenshots of those, in case you want to fix them. I did not encounter a single gameplay bug though, so good job on testing
Another thing I liked was that you tried to put some dialogue on most of the things just lying around (and more than just "It's an empty barrel"). I think that's pretty important to add some atomsphere. Also the elevators looked pretty cool with this 3D effect.
So yeah, all that aside, as I said, I had a lot of fun with this short demo and I am looking forward to the Full Version. Did not manage to beat Saci without using the pollution solution, but during my playthrough I wasn't aware that this was even possible. I read about it in your description just yet, after playing.
Thanks for creating this game, keep up the good work!
